AI is not a tool you will be asked to explore here. It is the default. You are expected to prototype, automate, and iterate using AI natively from day one.


WHAT YOU'LL OWN

  • Own the full growth loop: Activation Engagement Habit Formation Retention for DBMCI One learners across platforms.
  • Define and drive the product roadmap for learner-facing features, from discovery through experimentation, launch, and post-launch iteration.
  • Use AI-assisted prototyping and vibe-coding tools to independently build and test product ideas, reducing dependence on full engineering cycles for early validation.
  • Design and run GTM experiments: scope the hypothesis, build a lean version, get it in front of real users, gather feedback, and iterate fast before committing to a full build.
  • Design and run A/B experiments at pace. Test hypotheses, kill what does not work, and double down on what does.
  • Conduct structured user research: interviews, session analysis, and cohort studies to uncover the real reasons learners drop off or stay hooked.
  • Identify leading indicators of learner success and build features that move them, not vanity metrics.
  • Use agentic AI and automation workflows to accelerate research synthesis, user feedback analysis, and product iteration cycles.
  • Write crisp PRDs, define acceptance criteria, and partner with Engineering and Design through the full delivery cycle.
  • Own the metrics framework for your charter. Build dashboards, present to leadership, and stay fully accountable for outcomes.
  • Work closely with the Content and Academics teams to ensure product and pedagogy reinforce each other.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

  • 2 to 4 years of Product Management experience at a tech-first company. Consumer internet, EdTech, or mobile-first products are strongly preferred.
  • Strong product thinking grounded in user behaviour. You can articulate the "why behind the why" for any user action or drop-off.
  • Hands-on data fluency: SQL, funnel analysis, cohort analysis, and A/B experiment design. You live in data, not just talk about it.
  • AI fluency is non-negotiable. Proficient with AI-assisted prototyping and vibe-coding tools (Cursor, Bolt, Lovable, Replit, or similar). Practical experience with agentic AI workflows, automation, and prompt engineering applied to product work.
  • Technical fluency: You can hold a system design conversation with Engineering, understand API dependencies, and make informed build-vs-scope decisions.
  • Proven ability to run end-to-end GTM experiments: scope, build, launch, gather user feedback, and iterate with speed and structure.
  • First-principles thinker. You do not copy-paste frameworks; you reason from the user and the context up.
  • High ownership, low excuses. You move fast, learn faster, and take full responsibility for what ships and what it achieves.
  • Clear, structured communicator. You can align a cross-functional team with a well-framed problem statement and a sharp point of view.

jobDescription:
JOB DESCRIPTION
Job Title : AVP - DC Automation
Company : BDx India Pvt Ltd
Department : IT
Position Reporting to : Innovation Head
Location : India

ROLE SUMMARY
The Assistant Vice President of Data Center Automation is a senior leadership role responsible for driving the automation, optimization, and security of data center operations. This position oversees Building Management System (BMS) operations, and OSS/BSS (Operational Support Systems/Business Support Systems) functions, ensuring seamless integration, efficiency, and resilience across all systems. The ideal candidate will possess a strong technical background, strategic vision, and proven experience in managing large-scale data center and telecom/IT service environments.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Technical Scope of Work
1. System Architecture Design - Must
  • Define and document the overall control architecture , including:
    • PLC/DDC network hierarchy and supervisory levels.
    • OT LAN segmentation, VLAN design, and IP plan.
    • Redundancy and failover logic for automation systems.
  • Develop IO lists , control philosophy documents and functional design specifications (FDS) .
  • Coordinate between MEP consultants , controls contractors , and operations to align automation design.
2. Control System Development - Must
  • Author control sequence logic for:
    • Power systems: Need to have good understanding of the capacity framework and working design of UPS, LV/MV switchgear, gensets, fuel systems, PDUs
    • Cooling systems: Need to have good understanding of the capacity framework and working design of chillers, CRAHs, pumps, valves, cooling towers, heat exchangers.
  • Configure and validate PLCs, DDCs, and SCADA servers (Schneider / Siemens / Rockwell / Honeywell).
  • Standardize data points and naming conventions across all systems.
  • Implement interoperability via BACnet/IP, Modbus TCP/IP, OPC-UA , and MQTT brokers for telemetry aggregation.
3. Commissioning Validation - Must
  • Develop FAT/SAT scripts for validation of control logic, redundancy, and failover scenarios.
  • Execute alarm and trend validation to ensure full functional coverage.
  • Oversee integration testing with DCIM , AIops , or energy optimization platforms.
4. OT Cybersecurity Governance - Great to Have
  • Define the OT framework for automation systems, including:
    • Network segregation between IT and OT.
    • Firewall and DMZ policy enforcement.
    • Patch management and backup strategy for controllers and servers.
  • Align systems to IEC 62443 or equivalent cybersecurity compliance framework.
  • Maintain system access logs , firmware inventories, and security posture reports.
5. Operations Enablement - Must
  • Create OM procedures for BMS / SCADA systems including:
    • Change management and version control.
    • Alarm rationalization and escalation protocols.
    • Data historian configuration and retention policies.
  • Develop automation analytics dashboards to track PUE, thermal KPIs, and predictive maintenance metrics.
6. Continuous Optimization - Must
  • Collaborate with design and operations teams to:
    • Tune PID loops and optimize control setpoints.
    • Integrate AI models for predictive control.
    • Support digital twin deployment and data validation.
Deliverables
  • Control Philosophy Document (CPD)
  • Functional Design Specification (FDS)
  • Control System Architecture Network Diagram
  • FAT/SAT Test Protocols Reports
  • OT Security Policy for Automation Systems
  • Standardized Tag List Alarm Database
QUALIFICATION EXPERIENCE
- Bachelor's degree in engineering or equivalent practical experience, Mechanical, Electrical or Controls degree preferred.
- Excellent understanding of industry-standard electrical and mechanical systems used in data centers, as well as controls/monitoring systems.
- Experience of 15 + years in designing, configuring, programming, installing, troubleshooting or servicing HVAC Controls and Electrical SCADA systems application specific controllers, Building Management System (BMS) Controls software and networks.
- Develop and modify controls logic programming and graphical user interfaces.
- Manage multiple stakeholder deliverables, requirements and navigate challenging situations.
- Project coordination experience with multiple teams or vendors to meet project requirements for data centers.
- TCP/IP, MQTT, BACnet and/or MODBUS communication protocol experience.
- Proficient with Microsoft Office Suite and project management software.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Quality Engineering
jobDescription:
Your Role

As a Senior Software Engineer on the Platform team, you will build and own the frameworks, tooling, and CI/CD infrastructure that let Alpaca s engineers ship new features quickly and reliably. This is a software engineering role at its core: you will spend most of your time writing Go, designing automated test frameworks, and digging into application code and Kubernetes when needed. Just as importantly, you will help redefine how we use AI to raise the bar on quality - leveraging LLMs and AI-driven tooling to generate tests, catch regressions before they ship, and turn every incident into durable, automated coverage. We are looking for engineers who treat quality as an engineering discipline and see AI as a force multiplier for it - people who build the systems that make testing fast, reliable, and effortless for the teams that depend on them.

Things You Get To Do
  • Design and build automated test frameworks across our REST and gRPC API surface.
  • Leverage AI and LLM-based tooling to accelerate test generation, harden regression coverage, and turn production incidents into automated tests - embedding these practices into the frameworks the whole engineering org relies on.
  • Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines - we use a mix of GitHub Actions and Google Cloud Build.
  • Design and execute load, stress, and scalability tests to ensure our platform can handle growing demand.
  • Introduce chaos engineering practices - designing fault-injection and resilience experiments that surface failure modes before our customers do.
  • Standardize tooling and infrastructure to improve the day-to-day developer experience.
  • Partner with other teams to raise test coverage, reliability, and speed across services.
  • Dig into application code to root-cause failures and drive fixes to completion.
  • Mentor and guide product engineers, fostering a culture of quality and continuous improvement.
Who You Are (Must-Haves)
  • You have 5+ years of experience as a software engineer building and maintaining production systems.
  • You have written code in strongly typed languages and have at least 1 year of experience with Go.
  • You are fluent with AI-assisted engineering - you actively use LLM-based tools in your workflow and have a clear point of view on where they elevate quality (and where they don t).
  • You have built and maintained CI pipelines before - ideally with GitHub Actions or Google Cloud Build.
  • You have designed and built automated test frameworks, and you understand the challenges microservices pose for reliable integration and end-to-end testing.
  • You are familiar with Kubernetes beyond the basics - you can write a Helm chart for a new service with relative ease, you understand best practices around security, and you have prior job experience or certifications to prove this.
  • You have worked at a startup before - you understand that things don t always go according to plan, that there is significant technical debt, that some tasks just need to be done, and that sometimes there are no processes or documentation to guide your hand.
  • You are not afraid of taking a task from start to finish - gathering requirements, figuring out and implementing the best technical solution, then deploying and monitoring the results.
Who You Might Be (Bonus Points)
  • You have used AI/LLM tooling to build QA automation - test generation, flaky-test triage, or incident-to-regression pipelines - and can speak to what worked and what didn t.
  • You have written code in Python or TypeScript, and can build efficient Dockerfiles and secure container images.
  • You have implemented load tests with k6 (REST) and ghz (gRPC) and have experience analyzing pprof/trace output.
  • You have done IaC deployments with Argo CD or Terraform, or have used Google Cloud Platform and Google Kubernetes Engine before. You are familiar with Tilt and have written a Kubernetes Operator before.
  • You have practiced chaos engineering - running fault-injection or resilience experiments with tools like Chaos Mesh, LitmusChaos, or Gremlin.
  • You are familiar with testing event-driven systems using Kafka (or even better, Redpanda).

title: MQ Systems Administration Specialist
jobDescription:
Job Summary
We are currently seeking a MQ Systems Administration Specialist to join our team in Bangalore, KarnAtaka (IN-KA), India (IN).
Role Summary
NTT DATA is seeking -- years of experienced Enterprise Messaging Integration Engineer is responsible for designing, implementing, administering, and supporting enterprise-grade messaging, integration, and workload automation platforms. This role ensures secure, reliable, high-performance communication between distributed applications using IBM, Apache, and open-source messaging technologies. The engineer also manages complex scheduling environments and contributes to automation, observability, and continuous improvement of mission critical integration systems.
Key Responsibilities
  • Messaging Platform Administration (IBM MQ, Kafka, ActiveMQ, RabbitMQ): Install, configure, upgrade, and secure messaging platforms. Create and manage messaging artifacts: queue managers, queues, topics, channels, listeners, security settings, retention policies. Implement HA/DR, clustering, replication, and multi-node failover strategies. Performance tuning: throughput optimization, message persistence, batch sizes, connection pools, buffer/log tuning. Monitor health metrics using dashboards (Prometheus/Grafana/ELK/Splunk) and handle incidents proactively. Troubleshoot message flow failures, dead-letter queues, consumer lag, stuck messages, and network bottlenecks.
  • Integration Engineering (IBM IIB / ACE): Design, develop, and deploy message flows using ESQL, Java, mapping nodes, REST/SOAP connectors, MQ/Kafka nodes. Build and manage BAR files, integration nodes, servers, policies, and environment overrides. Implement integration security: TLS/mTLS, OAuth/JWT, Basic Auth, certificate management. Troubleshoot and optimize integration flows for latency, throughput, parser efficiency, and memory footprint. Participate in CI/CD pipelines, automated deployments, unit testing, and environment migrations.
  • IoT Telemetry Messaging (IBM MQXR / MQTT): Configure and support MQXR Telemetry listeners, MQTT topics, subscriptions, and QoS policies. Secure MQTT clients using TLS certificates, access control, and throttling policies. Monitor MQTT client connections, sessions, retained messages, and message routing to backend MQ systems.
  • Workload Automation (IBM TWS / IWS): Install, upgrade, configure, and administer TWS/IWS masters, controllers, and agents. Build job streams, calendars, dependencies, event triggers, and SLA monitoring. Troubleshoot job failures, optimize schedules, and implement recovery workflows. Integrate workload scheduler with MQ, REST APIs, databases, file systems, and enterprise applications.
  • Security, Governance Compliance: Implement end to end security for messaging and integration technologies: TLS/SSL, mTLS, JAAS, CHLAUTH policies, RBAC, OAuth/SASL. Perform auditing reporting for security compliance frameworks. Ensure platform hardening, certificate rotation, and vulnerability remediation.
  • Automation, DevOps Observability: Create automation scripts (Shell, Python, PowerShell) for deployments, housekeeping, and monitoring. Build IaC templates (Ansible, Terraform) for consistent provisioning. Integrate platforms into CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, Azure DevOps, GitLab CI). Maintain dashboards for real time system health and SLA adherence.
  • Documentation Collaboration: Create runbooks, SOPs, operational guidelines, and architectural diagrams. Work closely with application teams, architects, network, cloud, and security teams. Participate in on call rotation and production support responsibilities.
Required Skills Experience
  • IBM MQ (Distributed / MQ Clustering / Security)
  • IBM IIB/ACE development administration
  • IBM TWS/IWS job scheduling
  • MQTT / MQXR messaging
  • Apache Kafka (brokers, topics, partitions, ACLs, Schema Registry)
  • Apache ActiveMQ (Classic/Artemis)
  • RabbitMQ (AMQP, mirrored/quorum queues, federation/shovel)
  • Strong Linux/Unix system administration skills.
  • Strong debugging skills across messaging, network, TLS, and application layers.
  • Good understanding of networking (TCP/IP, firewalls, load balancers, proxies).
Good-to-Have Skills
  • Experience with Kubernetes (OpenShift/EKS/AKS) for containerized messaging platforms.
  • Cloud messaging equivalents (Azure Event Hub, AWS MQ/Kinesis/SNS/SQS, GCP Pub/Sub).
  • Experience with microservices and event-driven architectures.
  • Exposure to CI/CD, GitOps, Infrastructure-as-Code.
  • Monitoring tool exposure
Soft Skills Competencies
  • Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills
  • Good documentation and communication skills
  • Customer-focused approach
  • Ability to work in global teams
  • Ability to work in 24/7 support rotations when required.
  • Risk identification and proactive mitigation mindset
Educational Qualifications

  • Relevant certifications (if any) preferred

Job Title
AI Orchestration / Platform Engineer
Job Details
  • Number of positions: 1
  • Level: Senior / Lead Platform Individual Contributor
  • Primary locations: Hyderabad or Noida preferred; exceptional onshore candidates may be considered
  • Target / alternate titles: AI Platform Engineer; Agent Platform Engineer; LLMOps Engineer; GenAI Platform Engineer; AI DevOps Engineer; AI Site Reliability Engineer; ML Platform Engineer

  • Recruiter red flags: Traditional DevOps profile with no AI runtime understanding; framework-only orchestration without production platform depth; manual deployments; no observability or incident ownership; cannot explain model routing, state, retries, evaluation, or AI-specific controls.
Job Summary
Role purpose: Build and operate the orchestration and runtime capabilities that allow agentic applications to move reliably from development into production. The role will integrate agent workflows with existing cloud, security, policy, CI/CD, and observability capabilities, supporting multi-step execution, model routing, state, resiliency, evaluation, and production operations without rebuilding the client's established platform foundations.
Client and delivery context: The client already has delivery pipelines, policy-based architecture, security controls, and production review processes. The engineer must integrate with and enhance those capabilities. The platform should support multiple models, clouds, frameworks, and developer-productivity ecosystems without forcing avoidable lock-in. The engineer will support shared patterns used across different business-process agents and may work across two parallel delivery tracks. Platform work must be pragmatic and outcome-driven, with emphasis on enabling engineers to release and operate reliable agents quickly.
Primary ownership: Agent workflow and runtime orchestration, including state, routing, queues, retries, timeouts, scheduling, persistence, and exception management. Model gateway and routing patterns, provider abstraction, policy-based selection, fallback, rate limits, quotas, and cost controls. CI/CD, environment promotion, configuration, secrets, infrastructure integration, release validation, rollback, and operational readiness. Application and platform observability, reliability engineering, incident response, capacity, performance, and production support.
Responsibilities

We are currently seeking a MCP and Enterprise Integration Engineer to join our team in Hyderabad, Telangana (IN-TG), India (IN).
MCP and Enterprise Integration Engineer
Model Context Protocol | Enterprise tools and APIs | Secure, reusable integration
Position details
  • Number of positions: 1
  • Level: Senior Individual Contributor
  • Primary locations: Hyderabad or Noida preferred; exceptional onshore candidates may be considered

Role purpose
Design, build, secure, and operate MCP servers, tools, and enterprise-integration components that allow agents to interact safely with business systems, data platforms, knowledge sources, and operational services. The role will establish reusable tool contracts and integration patterns that can be extended by internal teams as new ecosystems and use cases are added.
Client and delivery context
The first MCP server and tools create the pattern for broader scale. Once the scaffolding is proven, internal teams should be able to add tools with lower effort and risk.
The client already applies strong review and security scrutiny to production MCP services. The engineer must produce implementation and evidence that can pass established controls.
Integrations may span service management, identity, configuration data, knowledge bases, data platforms, business applications, and custom internal APIs.
The engineer must understand both agent behavior and traditional enterprise integration; tool exposure must not bypass business rules, authorization, or auditability.
Primary ownership
  • MCP server architecture and implementation, tool and resource definitions, schemas, discovery, versioning, lifecycle management, and developer documentation.
  • Secure connectivity to enterprise systems, including authentication, authorization, secrets, service identities, network controls, and data access enforcement.

  • Tool-level observability, testing, error management, performance, resilience, and reusable implementation patterns.

  • Implement input validation, output normalization, idempotency, retries, timeouts, rate limits, circuit breakers, pagination, caching, and consistent error contracts.
  • Prevent unsafe tool use through explicit schemas, server-side business rules, authorization checks, confirmation patterns, and restricted action surfaces.
  • Create contract, integration, security, performance, and end-to-end tests for MCP tools and downstream dependencies.
  • Instrument tool calls with tracing, metrics, structured logs, audit events, latency, failure reasons, and dependency health.
  • Support deployment, release management, version compatibility, rollback, incident troubleshooting, and production support for MCP services.
  • Publish reusable SDKs, templates, tool-development guidance, examples, and onboarding documentation for internal teams.
Must-have candidate profile

jobDescription:
About J-PAL South Asia:
J-PAL is a global research centre working to reduce poverty and fight climate change by ensuring that policy is informed by scientific evidence. Anchored by a network of over 1,100 researchers at universities across the world, J-PAL works with governments, NGOs, and donors to generate evidence and scale effective solutions. J-PAL South Asia, based at the Institute for Financial Management and Research (IFMR) in Chennai, leads J-PAL s efforts to advance evidence-informed policymaking across the region. The office works with over 20 state governments and multiple central ministries in India, across sectors including health, education, labour markets, energy, environment, climate action, and gender.
J-PAL South Asia hosts CLEAR South Asia, the Regional Centre for Learning on Evaluation and Results, coordinated by the World Bank s Independent Evaluation Group (IEG). CLEAR South Asia is a key implementing partner of the Global Evaluation Initiative (GEI), a global network of institutions dedicated to strengthening evaluation capacities in developing countries.
About the Training Vertical:
The Training vertical at J-PAL South Asia works to strengthen monitoring, evaluation, data, and evidence-use capacities and systems. The team delivers open-enrolment and customised courses, technical advisory services, fellowships, knowledge products, and long-term institutional capacity-building engagements with governments and other development partners. J-PAL South Asia also hosts CLEAR South Asia, a key implementing partner of the Global Evaluation Initiative.
Role Summary:
J-PAL South Asia seeks a data-focused Training Manager / Senior Manager to lead the design and delivery of capacity-building programmes that help public institutions and social-sector organisations improve how they collect, manage, analyse, govern, and use data for decision-making and evaluation. The role sits at the intersection of applied data analytics, monitoring and evaluation, adult learning, and institutional strengthening.
The successful candidate will translate real-world administrative and programme data challenges into rigorous, practice-oriented curricula and advisory engagements. They will lead technical content development, facilitate training for diverse audiences, manage partnerships and programmes, mentor team members, and help build a portfolio of data-capacity initiatives that is closely connected to J-PAL s research and policy mission.
Key Responsibilities:
  • Data-focused training strategy and portfolio development
    • Support the development and execution of the Training vertical s strategy for data and evidence capacity building, translating priorities into annual plans, milestones, budgets, and measurable outcomes.
    • Contribute to thought leadership on the evolving role of data systems, AI, and digital tools in M&E practice, helping government partners navigate opportunities and risks as these technologies reshape how evidence is generated and used in public systems.
    • Identify opportunities for new courses, technical assistance, fellowships, and institutional partnerships focused on administrative data, data governance, analytics, and evidence use.
    • Build a coherent pathway from foundational data literacy to advanced applied analytics, tailored to the needs of government officials, M&E practitioners, researchers, and implementing organisations.
    • Contribute to fundraising, proposal development, donor engagement, and the stewardship of existing grants.
  • Curriculum and technical content development
    • Lead the design, adaptation, and quality assurance of curricula, teaching materials, exercises, datasets, manuals, toolkits, and knowledge products on data-focused topics.
    • Develop applied learning content using realistic government and social-sector datasets, while ensuring confidentiality, ethical use, and appropriate data protection.
    • Create training modules for partners on topics such as data quality assessment, data cleaning and validation, reproducible workflows, administrative data systems, data visualisation, dashboarding, data governance, responsible data use, and the use of data for monitoring and evaluation.
    • Translate technical concepts into accessible and engaging learning experiences for audiences with different levels of quantitative proficiency.
    • Keep content current by drawing on J-PAL research, field experience, partner needs, and emerging good practices in public-interest data systems.
  • Training delivery and facilitation
    • Lead and facilitate high-quality in-person, virtual, and blended training programmes for government and non-government stakeholders.
    • Teach technical sessions and oversee hands-on labs using relevant software such as Excel, Stata, R, Python, SQL, or data-visualisation tools.
    • Design assessments, assignments, capstone exercises, and feedback mechanisms that measure learning and application rather than participation alone.
    • Coach other trainers and subject-matter experts to ensure consistency, accuracy, strong pedagogy, and an inclusive learner experience.
  • Technical advisory and institutional data-capacity strengthening
    • Work with state and central government partners, civil society organisations, and other institutions to diagnose data-system and analytical-capacity gaps.
    • Translate partner needs into feasible technical assistance plans, including data-quality protocols, documentation standards, reporting frameworks, analytical workflows, and capacity-building roadmaps.
    • Advise partners on strengthening data collection, metadata, data dictionaries, codebooks, validation rules, reproducible analysis, and responsible data-sharing practices.
    • Support partners to move from one-off analysis towards institutionalised routines for monitoring, learning, and evidence-informed decision-making.
    • Coordinate with J-PAL s research and policy teams to identify data assets and problem statements that may support future research or evaluation opportunities.
  • Programme and partnership management
    • Manage multiple training and advisory engagements end to end, including scoping, work planning, staffing, contracting, delivery, risk management, reporting, and close-out.
    • Build and maintain trusted relationships with senior government officials, donors, universities, technical partners, and civil society organisations.
    • Ensure programmes are responsive to partner needs while maintaining J-PAL s standards for technical quality and ethical data use.
    • Represent the Training vertical in external meetings, workshops, and ecosystem convenings.
  • Learning, knowledge management, and evidence of programme effectiveness
    • Develop monitoring, evaluation, and learning frameworks for data-capacity programmes, tracking learning gains, application of skills, institutional adoption, and improvements in data practices.
    • Create and maintain reusable repositories of curricula, code examples, teaching datasets, templates, case studies, and delivery guidance.
    • Lead the production of practical briefs, case notes, playbooks, and donor-facing learning products that document what works in strengthening institutional data capacity.
    • Use learner and partner feedback to continuously improve programme design and delivery.
  • Team leadership and organisational contribution
    • Supervise, mentor, and support Training Associates, Senior Training Associates, consultants as the need may be.
    • Set clear goals and quality standards, review technical outputs, and support the professional development of team members.
    • Contribute to financial and operational management, grant reporting, recruitment, and cross-vertical organisational initiatives.
    • Promote a collaborative culture that combines technical rigour, practical problem-solving, and strong partner orientation.
Minimum Qualifications:
  • Master s degree in economics, statistics, data science, computer science and AI, engineering or a related quantitative or social science field.
  • For Manager: at least 5 years of relevant professional experience. For Senior Manager: typically 7 or more years of relevant experience, including substantial programme or team leadership.
  • Demonstrated experience using data for public policy, monitoring and evaluation, social-impact programmes, government advisory, or applied research.
  • Strong applied data-analysis skills and proficiency in at least one statistical programming language such as R, or Python; working knowledge of SQL is strongly preferred.
  • Experience working with large, messy, or administrative datasets, including data cleaning, validation, documentation, analysis, and visualisation.

title: District Coordinator - Rural Growth Hub
jobDescription:
Designation- District Coordinator - Rural Growth Hub
Programme- Strengthening Indias Agricultural Transformation- Rural Growth Hub Pilots
Reporting To- PMU Lead
Engagement Type- Fixed-term Employment
Locations (One Position for Each Location)- Bachhwara, Begusarai (Bihar) | Pallahara, Angul (Odisha) | Maregaon, Yavatmal (Maharashtra) | Indora, Kangra (Himachal Pradesh)

Vision for the Role
Athena Infonomics is supporting the NITI Aayog in the design and implementation of the Rural Growth Hub (RGH) programme- a three-year field engagement demonstrating how integrated, convergence-led agricultural transformation can be achieved at the village cluster level. The programme operates across five states - Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Odisha, Maharashtra, and Himachal Pradesh- with one pilot district and one focus block per state.
The RGH is the operational centrepiece of this engagement. It brings together government schemes, frontier technologies, community institutions, and market linkages within a single village cluster as mutually reinforcing components of a coherent local development system. Rather than adding another layer to an already crowded programme landscape, the RGH works through what already exists: mapping farmers to schemes they are eligible for but not accessing, embedding technologies within existing government delivery channels, and strengthening the capacity of frontline officials to coordinate more effectively. The programme sits within a broader national architecture. PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PM-DDKY) provide a reference framework for scheme convergence across 100 aspirational agricultural districts that RGH could learn from and inform. The upcoming Rural Prosperity and Resilience Programme (RPRP) is expected to provide a future financing pathway for scaling what the RGH pilots demonstrate.


The District Coordinator is Athenas single point of contact at the district and focus block level across all concerned departments. This is the role of the primary field intelligence anchor - someone sufficiently embedded in the district and block ecosystem to understand what is happening in practice, what are the opportunities for convergence and what needs to be enabled to make it happen, and how the RGH model can credibly strengthen farmer, village, and block-level outcomes. The District Coordinators ground-level judgement and documentation are the raw material from which the programme learns.


What You Will Own
  • Ground-level intelligence: a current, granular understanding of the agricultural and rural livelihoods landscape in your district and focus block - going beyond administrative data to understand what is happening in practice, how frontline officials are operating, and where scheme intent diverges from farmer experience, existing adoption level of technologies and the market for such services.
  • District and block action plan engagement: systematic gathering and analysis of the District Agriculture and Allied Activities Plan (DAAP) and block-level action plans wherever they exist, and contribution to the design of the Village Cluster Agriculture Action Plan (VCAAP) - the shared planning instrument anchoring the RGH cluster.
  • Intervention mapping, validation, and orchestration: a comprehensive, honest assessment of all active interventions in the focus block - government schemes, technology pilots, and civil society activities - evaluating what is working for which farmer profiles and documenting clearly where it is not. The role is primarily to inform the larger orchestration efforts towards matchmaking, prioritisations, additional activities to amplify impact by different stakeholders.
  • Stakeholder interface: Establish and manager primary working relationship with the District Collectors, District and Block Agriculture / Horticulture Officers, BDO, DPM-RL, Village Pradhans, Panchayat Secretaries, CRPs, KVK staff, and NRLM field functionaries - convening cluster coordination meetings and tracking scheme enrolment, delivery timelines, and institutional bottlenecks. The role also requires engagement with officials at the state level on areas where state level institutions, infrastructure and digital initiatives could be leveraged for scale up.
  • Technical and process documentation: weekly field observation logs, structured farmer feedback records, convergence opportunity matrices, technology adoption data, and monthly field intelligence reports - the mechanism through which ground-level learning becomes evidence that shapes programme adaptation and national policy.

Key Responsibilities

Scheme convergence and farmer-level mapping
  • Map every farmer in the RGH cluster to their current scheme enrolment status, eligibility gaps, and access barriers, building a convergence opportunity matrix per farmer profile and season. Build a strong and contextual understanding of focus schemes including underlying issues and challenges, areas for improvement etc.
  • Coordinate with block and district line department officers to unlock scheme access for eligible farmers, with particular attention to women farmers, SHG members, and marginal landholders. Track progress weekly against the programme target of a minimum of five schemes per farmer in the cluster.
Frontier technology assessment and deployment support
  • Assess existing frontier technology deployments in the focus block - drones, AI advisory systems, soil health tools, precision irrigation, digital crop surveys - evaluating adoption rates, farmer experience, and input efficiency outcomes.
  • Support identification and validation of additional technologies to be layered on existing interventions if any, ensuring they are embedded within government delivery systems and that data collection protocols meet programme standards.
Ground intelligence and field reporting
  • Maintain weekly field observation logs and prepare monthly field intelligence reports synthesising what is working, what is not, and what course corrections are needed.
  • Oversee conduction of structured farmer feedback sessions at the midline and endline, contributing to the programmes baseline-midline-endline survey framework and the generation of outcome data on farm income, yield, input costs, and market access.
  • Travel between the District Headquarters and Blocks as needed with a focus on project outputs and outcomes rather than activities.
Data systems and Shared Data Map maintenance
  • Maintain and update the Shared Data Map - the field-level data convergence instrument to ensure clarity on what data systems, parameters exist including information on data quality, validation status etc.
Community institution strengthening
  • Engage with SHG leads and KVK extension staff to assess the institutional capacity of community organisations around collective scheme enrolment, market linkage, and technology adoption and identify areas of support.

Additional Responsibilities

In addition to responsibilities under the Rural Growth Hub (RGH) Project, the selected candidate will be expected to support and contribute to other ongoing projects, assignments, and initiatives undertaken by Athena Infonomics in the state, as and when required. Such responsibilities may include project planning, stakeholder coordination, data collection and analysis, reporting, field implementation support, and any other tasks aligned with the candidates role, skills, and organizational priorities.

Who We Think You Are
You are likely to have between six and ten years of experience working at district /block / state level in agriculture, rural development, livelihoods, or related fields. You may have come through a social enterprise, an NGO, a government programme implementation role, a development consultancy, or a technology-for-development organisation. What matters most is whether you have spent substantive time at the district level collaborating with frontline officials, community institutions, and farmer households - and whether you understand how government actually works in the states where this programme operates.


You are genuinely curious about why things do not work. When a scheme is not reaching farmers, you want to understand the precise point at which it breaks down. You do not accept low awareness as a sufficient explanation. You have the patience to sit with a Block Agriculture Officer or a Panchayat Secretary and understand their actual operating constraints, not their official account of them. You write clearly - field reports that are honest about what did not work, specific about why, and clear about what it implies. You are at ease in a programme designed to learn and adapt rather than to deliver a fixed model.


WHAT WE EXPECT YOU TO BRING
  • A postgraduate qualification in agriculture, rural development, public policy, economics, social work, or a related discipline is the minimum educational requirement.
  • Between six and ten years of work experience, with at least three years in a district or block-level role in agriculture, rural livelihoods, or a related programme.
  • Direct prior experience of working with state government departments - particularly those relevant to agriculture, rural development, and livelihoods - in the state of the district you are applying for. This is a requirement, not a preference.
  • Demonstrated experience of working across a multi-stakeholder ecosystem comprising government line departments, self-help groups, civil society organisations, and private sector service providers.
  • Working familiarity with at least one government scheme MIS or data system - e.g., the NRLM portal, PM-KISAN, PM KUSUM, PMKSY, PM-DDKY, PMFBY, AgriStack, or equivalent - at an operational level.
  • Strong written communication skills in English and in the native language of the district of posting.
  • Exposure to frontier technologies in agriculture is an advantage, though not a prerequisite.

What Athena Offers
The District Coordinator role sits at the most consequential part of Athenas work - the point at which research, policy, and technology meet the reality of a farmers field. The programme is a national engagement with NITI Aayog, supported by a leading philanthropic organisation, and designed to generate evidence that informs how India approaches agricultural transformation at scale. The field intelligence you produce will feed directly into the formulation and design of the RGH models across the focus blocks.

You will work closely with the central PMU team at NITI Aayog and Athena s Core Project Team, with regular structured feedback and cross-district learning cycles built into the programme design. Athena is investing in building its agriculture, climate, and livelihoods practice into a substantive national and international portfolio. For the right candidate, this role offers a genuine pathway into a growing organisation that values people who understand what is happening on the ground.

  • Competitive compensation benchmarked to development sector norms for district-level technical roles.
  • Travel support for district and block-level field visits and quarterly cross-district learning sessions.
  • Access to Athenas central research, data, and technology capabilities, including the APLYD AI and digital public infrastructure unit and the TolaData impact monitoring platform.
  • Structured mentorship from the central PMU team, with opportunities to growth within Athenas agriculture, climate, and livelihoods practice. [1]

Application Requirements
Please note that the selected candidates would be stationed at the identified block within the district with frequent travel to the District Headquarter.
  • Updated CV - not exceeding three pages.
  • A covering note (maximum four hundred words) on: which block you are applying for, your most relevant prior experience, and one observation from your field experience that you believe is underappreciated in how agricultural programmes are designed or how frontier technologies could witness accelerated adoption in the country.

Athena Infonomics is an Equal Opportunities Employer

Athena Infonomics is an equal opportunity employer with a commitment to diversity. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, protected veteran status, or disability status.

title: Sr Frontend Engineer
jobDescription:
About Us
Aivar Innovations is an AI-native services company and AWS Preferred Partner building governed, production-grade agentic AI systems. We partner with enterprises to deploy intelligent agents that automate complex business processes-from intelligent customer interactions to enterprise knowledge systems.

Experience: 4-8 years | 4+ years building complex, data-intensive or enterprise-grade frontend applications

The Role: You own major parts of the Kubogent frontend end to end: the control surface platform teams, M
L engineers, and application teams use to manage Kubernetes infrastructure, build AI/ML workloads, inspect experiments, operate models,
and understand what is happening across their environments.

Kubogent is not a conventional CRUD application. The frontend includes cluster and GPU management, project workspaces, notebooks, experiments, training and inference workflows, pipeline visualisation, live logs and events, browser terminals, model playgrounds, analytics, and administrative surfaces. You will take ambiguous product problems, decide how they should work, prototype the interaction model, and ship the result.

What youll do
  • Own complex product surfaces. Build and evolve dashboards, resource explorers, workflow editors, experiment views, model-serving interfaces, project workspaces, and administrative consoles used across the Kubogent platform.
  • Design it, then build it. There is no requirement that every feature arrives as a finished mockup. You take a product problem, understand the workflow, prototype an interaction model, and turn it into a polished production experience.
  • Own data-dense infrastructure views. Make clusters, nodes, GPUs, workloads, logs, events, quotas, experiments, and deployments understandable even when customers operate at significant scale.
  • Build real-time surfaces. Work with WebSockets, SSE, streaming logs, live status transitions, long-runningoperations, and high-frequency telemetry without compromising responsiveness or rendering performance.
  • Build interactive developer tools. Create experiences such as in-browser terminals, YAML/configuration editors,workflow or DAG visualisation, model playgrounds, notebook launch flows, and operational debugging interfaces.
  • Own frontend state architecture. Define patterns for server state, local state, optimistic updates, background refresh, async operations, error handling, and long-running workflow state.
  • Own the design system. Build reusable components, layout primitives, tokens, interaction patterns, and typedcontracts that keep the platform consistent as the product surface expands.
  • Shape multi-tenant UX. Make projects, organizations, clusters, permissions, roles, and resource boundaries clear to users without treating client-side checks as the security boundary.
  • Partner directly with backend and platform engineers. Influence API contracts, event models, pagination, filtering, workflow state machines, and product semantics rather than treating APIs as fixed inputs.
  • Keep the product fast. Establish performance budgets, profiling practices, virtualization strategies, bundlediscipline, and rendering patterns for large enterprise datasets.
  • Raise the production bar. Establish E2E coverage, frontend observability, error monitoring, test strategy, andrelease discipline.
  • Set the bar. Review code, mentor engineers, establish frontend standards, and help define what high-quality product engineering looks like at Aivar.

What were looking for
  • 4+ years building production frontend applications, with real depth in complex, data-intensive, infrastructure , developer-tooling , analytics, or enterprise products.
  • Deep React knowledge. Hooks, component architecture, rendering behaviour, memoization, state ownership, performance profiling, and the ability to explain why a component re-renders.
  • Strong TypeScript across UI components, API contracts, shared libraries, schemas, and application state.
  • You have built a genuinely hard product surface. Examples could include an IDE-like interface, workflow builder, graph editor, terminal, monitoring product, analytics console, infrastru cture dashboard, collaborative editor, or another interaction-heavy application.
  • You design, you dont just implement. You are comfortable starting from a workflow or product problem instead ofwaiting for final mocks.
  • Strong async-state fluency. WebSockets, SSE, polling, background jobs, live status updates, cancellation, retries,
  • reconnects, and partial failure.
  • Experience with data-dense interfaces. Filtering, sorting, pagination, virtualization, large tables, timelines, charts, logs, or event streams.
  • Design-system ownership. You have built or significantly evolved a component system other engineers relied on.
  • Strong API instincts. You can identify when an awkward frontend experience is actually caused by the wrong backend contract and work with backend engineers to fix it.
  • Production discipline. You have introduced or meaningfully improved E2E testing, CI, monitoring, performance measurement, or frontend reliability practices.
  • Comfort with cloud-native concepts. You do not need to be a Kubernetes expert, but concepts such as clusters, pods, deployments, namespaces, GPUs, jobs, logs, metrics, and RBAC should not intimidate you.
  • Fluency with agentic coding tools. We expect AI to carry routine implementation work so that you can spend moretime on architecture, interaction design, debugging, performance, and product decisions.

Strong pluses:
  • Experience building developer tools, cloud consoles, observability products, infrastruor internal developer platforms.
  • Monaco Editor, xterm.js, React Flow or similar graph/canvas libraries.
  • High-frequency charts, log viewers, terminal emulators, or workflow editors.
  • Experience with accessibility and keyboard-heavy power-user interfaces.
  • Familiarity with Kubernetes, MLflow, Argo Workflows, Ray, Prometheus, or similar infrastructure.

This role may not be the best match if:
  • Youprefer working primarily from predefined tickets and pixel-complete design handoffs. Were looking for someone who owns problems, drives solutions, and shapes the product.
  • Your experience is primarily marketing sites or straightforward CRUD applications. Kubogent has many highlystateful, real-time, infrastructure-heavy product surfaces.
  • You think frontend architecture ends at component structure. State models, API semantics, performance,workflows, failure states, and product interaction design are central to this role.

About the Role
The Principal Outcome Manager owns business outcomes for our clients - not just projects. This is a senior consulting role that combines deep technology fluency, strong business judgment and disciplined delivery leadership.
It is not a traditional project manager role. The Outcome Manager agrees with the client up-front on what success looks like in measurable terms, leads the team that delivers it, tracks the outcome continuously, and stands behind the realized result.
In one line: agree the outcome, deliver the outcome, and make sure both the client and Tezo win.

Key Responsibilities
1. Discovery and outcome definition
  • Run discovery workshops with client business and technology leaders to uncover the real problem.
  • Translate the clients ambition into 2-4 measurable KPIs with clear baselines and targets.
  • Document and sign off the outcome, the measurement method and the review cadence with the client.
2. Shaping the engagement
  • Partner with sales and pricing to structure a fair, outcome-linked commercial that protects margin and gives the client real upside.
  • Identify risks early and decide - with leadership - whether to pursue, reshape or decline the deal.
  • Co-own the Statement of Work, ensuring every outcome term is unambiguous and measurable.
3. Execution and delivery
  • Build the right cross-functional pod (architects, engineering leads, data scientists, analysts) and set the operating cadence.
  • Drive day-to-day delivery through the leads. You do not write code, but you always know whether the work is on track to the outcome - and intervene early when it is not.
  • Manage scope, risks, dependencies and change with discipline.
4. Outcome tracking and realization
  • Stand up a simple outcome dashboard for each engagement: live KPI values against baseline and target, with leading indicators.
  • Run a weekly internal review and a regular client-facing outcome review. Convert lagging KPIs into corrective actions with owners and dates.
  • Close each engagement with a short outcome memo: what was committed, what was delivered, what the business impact was, what to repeat next time.
5. Stakeholder consulting and communication
  • Act as a trusted advisor to client business and technology sponsors - bring point of view, not just status updates.
  • Translate fluently between the CIO/CTO conversation (architecture, data, AI, technical risk) and the CXO conversation (revenue, cost, customer experience, time-to-market).
  • Manage escalations and disagreements directly; protect the relationship and the outcome at the same time.
  • Identify the next outcome and help grow the account.

  • Coach engineering and consulting leads to think in outcomes rather than tasks.

title: Change Management Specialist
jobDescription:
Job Summary

The Change Management Specialist plays a critical role in ensuring strategic initiatives are successfully adopted across the organization. This role is responsible for developing and executing enterprise change strategies that drive stakeholder alignment, leadership engagement, organizational readiness, communications, capability building, and long-term adoption. Success in this role requires balancing people, process, and business priorities to help organizations realize the full value of transformation investments.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute end-to-end change strategies for enterprise transformation initiatives, ensuring successful adoption of new operating models, processes, technologies, and ways of working.
  • Integrate change management into program execution, aligning with business objectives, implementation roadmaps, and organizational priorities.
  • Assess organizational readiness by identifying adoption risks, stakeholder impacts, capability gaps, and resistance, and implement mitigation plans to ensure business readiness.
  • Consult govern enablement and adoption programs that equip employees to successfully transition to new ways of working.
  • Build stakeholder engagement and executive sponsorship strategies that drive alignment, commitment, and accountability across leadership and cross-functional teams.
  • Coach leaders on effective change leadership, communication, and stakeholder engagement throughout the transformation lifecycle.
  • Lead meaningful conversations with business leaders on transformation program governance, decision-making, and negotiating resolution, using strong business judgment, situational awareness, and executive presence to read the room, steer discussions toward desired outcomes, and flag issues or red flags early.
  • Develop and deliver executive communications, leadership messaging, presentations, toolkits, and communication plans that clearly articulate the transformation vision, business rationale, progress, and expected outcomes.
  • Ensure consistent, transparent, and aligned messaging across stakeholder groups.
  • Define and monitor change KPIs, adoption metrics, organizational health indicators, stakeholder sentiment, and training effectiveness to measure success and recommend improvements.
  • Partner with strategy, program management, HRBP, Communications, learning and development, technology, business operations, and executive leadership to align change activities with business priorities and execution timelines.
  • Establish scalable change management frameworks, governance, templates, and best practices that strengthen organizational change capability and support continuous improvement.

Requirements

  • 7-10 years of experience in Organizational Change Management, Business Transformation, Strategy, Program Management, Organizational Development, Human Capital Consulting, or Business Operations within a global technology or SaaS organization.
  • Bachelor s degree in business, Organizational Psychology, Human Resources, Communications, Management, or a related field; MBA or Masters preferred.
  • Proven experience leading enterprise-wide change initiatives, including organizational readiness, stakeholder engagement, executive communications, adoption, learning, and capability-building programs.
  • Strong expertise in change management frameworks such as PROSCI, ADKAR, Kotter, or equivalent methodologies.
  • Demonstrated success partnering with Director, VP, and Executive-level stakeholders, with exceptional facilitation, executive communication, and influencing skills.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities with experience measuring adoption, organizational health, and change effectiveness through defined KPIs and metrics.
  • Experience operating in highly matrixed, fast-paced organizations and collaborating across multiple business functions.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders in complex matrix environments, resolve conflict constructively, and bring strong business acumen and street-smart judgment to transformation governance discussions.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft 365 and modern collaboration platforms; experience using AI tools such as Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, or Claude to enhance communications, enablement, and change planning is highly desirable.

Preferred Qualifications

  • PROSCI Change Management, PMP, Agile, Lean, or equivalent professional certification.
  • Experience in Management Consulting (e.g., McKinsey, BCG, Bain, Deloitte, Accenture, EY, PwC, KPMG) or leading enterprise digital transformation, operating model redesign, organizational design, workforce transformation, or technology implementation initiatives.

Beyond the Resume

  • People-Centric Strategist: Drives successful transformation by balancing business objectives with organizational behaviour, culture, and employee experience.
  • Influential Leader: Builds trust, aligns diverse stakeholders, and drives adoption through collaboration rather than authority.
  • Executive Storyteller: Simplifies complex transformation into compelling narratives that inspire confidence and action.
  • Capability Builder: Creates scalable change frameworks, leadership capabilities, and organizational practices that sustain long-term transformation.
  • Data-Driven Change Leader: Uses adoption metrics, stakeholder insights, and organizational health indicators to measure success and continuously improve outcomes.
  • Thrives in Ambiguity: Brings structure, clarity, and confidence to fast-paced, evolving environments.
  • Continuous Learner: Embraces emerging change methodologies, AI-enabled tools, and workforce transformation practices to continuously enhance organizational effectiveness.

title: Sr Kubernetes Platform Engineer
jobDescription:
Job Summary

The Role: You build the Kubernetes substrate that makes Kubogent possible.

Kubogent is a Kubernetes-native AI infrastructure and MLOps platform. A central control plane manages multiple workload clusters, allocates infrastructure to tenants and projects, deploys platform capabilities on demand, runs GPU and ML workloads, exposes remote operational access, and continuously reconciles desired state with what is actually running.

This role is for someone who understands Kubernetes as a distributed system and programmable control plane, not just as a deployment target.

Responsibilities

  • Own Kubernetes control loops. Design and build CRDs, controllers, operators, reconcilers, finalizers, watches, status models, and lifecycle state machines using Go and controller-runtime.
  • Build multi-cluster control. Help design and implement how Kubogent onboards, authenticates, observes, upgrades, and controls workload clusters that may only initiate outbound connections to the control plane.
  • Build the workload-cluster agent. Own registration, heartbeat, inventory, command execution, reconnect behaviour, versioning, rollout, credential rotation, and failure recovery.
  • Translate platform intent into Kubernetes state. Convert concepts such as project placement, capabilities, resource allocation, model deployments, notebooks, training jobs, and shared services into safe, idempotent Kubernetes reconciliation.
  • Own resource isolation and placement. Work with namespaces, quotas, limits, priority, scheduling, taints/tolerations, affinity, topology, GPU resources, gang scheduling, and workload placement.
  • Build GPU and accelerator support. Integrate with NVIDIA GPU Operator, device plugins, MIG where appropriate, node feature discovery, topology-aware scheduling, and accelerator-specific runtime requirements.
  • Build secure remote operations. Design mechanisms for browser-based kubectl/exec/log access, tunneled cluster connectivity, least-privilege credentials, mTLS, authorization, and auditable command execution.
  • Own cluster capability deployment. Build mechanisms that install only the operators and services required by capabilities enabled on projects or clusters, rather than treating every cluster as identical.
  • Design for unreliable environments. Clusters disappear, links break, agents restart, watches expire, APIs throttle, upgrades partially fail, and reconciliation gets repeated. Your systems must remain correct anyway.
  • Work deeply with Kubernetes API machinery. Informers, watches, admission, status conditions, server-side apply, resource versions, optimistic concurrency, garbage collection, RBAC, and API conventions.
  • Own platform upgrades. Design safe version skew, agent upgrades, CRD evolution, migration, backward compatibility, and rollout/rollback strategies.
  • Drive observability for the platform itself. Instrument operators and agents with logs, metrics, traces, health checks, queue depth, reconciliation latency, and actionable failure signals.
  • Set the bar. Review designs and code, mentor engineers, and establish patterns for building reliable Kubernetes-native systems.

Requirements

  • Experience: 5-9 years | 4+ years building or operating production Kubernetes platforms, controllers, operators, or cloud-native infrastructure
  • 5+ years in software, platform, infrastructure, SRE, or cloud engineering, with substantial hands-on Kubernetes experience.
  • Strong Go. You should be comfortable designing production services, concurrency, interfaces, testing, profiling, and failure handling in Go.
  • Deep Kubernetes internals. Controllers, CRDs, reconciliation, API machinery, watches/informers, RBAC, admission, scheduling, storage, networking, and workload lifecycle.
  • You have built Kubernetes software, not only operated clusters. We especially value experience with Kubebuilder, controller-runtime, Operator SDK, custom schedulers, admission webhooks, or Kubernetes-integrated platforms.
  • Strong distributed-systems instincts. Idempotency, retries, at-least-once execution, eventual consistency, leases, leader election, partial failure, backpressure, and state convergence should be familiar ideas.
  • Experience operating Kubernetes across environments. Cloud-managed Kubernetes and on-prem/private-cloud experience are both valuable.
  • Comfort with networking. TCP/TLS, mTLS, proxies, reverse tunnels, WebSockets or streaming RPC, DNS, load balancers, ingress/gateway, and debugging connectivity failures.
  • Production troubleshooting ability. You can move from symptom to root cause across controllers, API servers, networking, scheduling, container runtimes, storage, and workloads.
  • Strong security fundamentals. Service identities, certificates, RBAC, secrets, credential rotation, least privilege, tenant isolation, and auditability.
  • Fluency with agentic coding tools. We expect AI to accelerate implementation and investigation while you remain responsible for architecture, correctness, failure handling, and operational quality.

Strong pluses

  • Multi-cluster management platforms.
  • Kubernetes API aggregation or extension patterns.
  • Cluster API, Crossplane, Argo CD, Flux, Rancher, Rafay, Open Cluster Management, or similar systems.
  • Envoy, reverse tunnels, relay systems, or secure remote cluster access.
  • GPU scheduling, NVIDIA GPU Operator, MIG, CUDA-aware workloads, or distributed training infra
  • Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, Loki, or Kubernetes observability stacks.
  • Kubernetes conformance, upgrade testing, chaos testing, or large-scale fleet management.

This role may not be the best match if

  • Your Kubernetes experience is primarily writing manifests, Helm charts, and maintaining CI/CD pipelines. We are building Kubernetes-native control-plane software.
  • You expect infrastructure to be reliable and synchronous. Disconnected clusters, duplicate commands, partial upgrades, stale state, and repeated reconciliation are normal operating conditions here.
  • You prefer solving platform problems by adding manual operational procedures. Kubogent must turn those procedures into productized, automated control loops.

title: Member of Technical Staff, Platform
jobDescription:
About Enterpret

At Enterpret, we are building the customer feedback intelligence platform that turns unstructured customer feedback into a structured, queryable source of truth - solving complex problems in natural language processing, serverless computing, and analytics on the frontend, pushing the envelope of whats possible by applying first principle thinking.

Kleiner Perkins and Sequoia Capital back us because they share our conviction that product development teams deserve a better way to understand their customers. That conviction is validated by the respected product teams who rely on us every day, including Canva, Notion, Samsung, and Loom.

We love working with folks who are resourceful, thrive in ambiguity, and display a strong sense of ownership.

Our engineering culture is built around leveraging and contributing to open-source tools. We aim to build upon and improve state-of-the-art systems in our field of work.

Read more about our team, core values, and operating principles - here .

What Youll Do
  • Design and deliver significant Graph Platform components end to end - high- and low-level design, implementation, rollout, and the follow-through after launch.
  • Improve reliability, latency, performance, and operational readiness across the knowledge graph, data systems such as DynamoDB and ClickHouse, Model Repository, LLM self-hosting platform, and the high-throughput pipelines that run our models.
  • Take production issues beyond the immediate symptom - turn recurring failures into durable fixes, not patches.
  • Build with metrics, alerts, runbooks, tests, and rollback plans as a core part of the work, so every change is safe and observable in production.
  • Own on-call and production responsibility for your area, and establish the operational baseline: failure modes, alerts, runbooks, and the gaps that need closing.
  • Partner with product engineers, product managers, SRE, and adjacent teams where your component has dependencies - and work closely with the people shaping the longer-term platform direction.
  • Continuously raise the engineering-quality bar through code review, testing, documentation, and support for more junior engineers.
What It Takes
  • 6+ years in software engineering, with evidence you can own a meaningful production component from conception to deployment.
  • 3+ years at one organization where youve designed, built, deployed, and operated a significant backend, data, or infrastructure component - not just shipped code, but kept it running well.
  • Comfort working through moderate ambiguity: you clarify unclear requirements, decide what needs to be built now, make design trade-offs across components, and deliver without constant direction.
  • Strong engineering-quality and operational habits: comprehensive tests, edge-case thinking, metrics, alerts, runbooks, rollback plans, and real production debugging experience.
  • Hands-on experience with high-throughput data systems or asynchronous pipelines - exposure to at least one of DynamoDB, ClickHouse, Snowflake, or model hosting/inferencing is valuable, and prior experience with Golang, Python, or another object-oriented programming language is preferred, though direct experience with our exact stack is not required.
  • An AI-native working style: you use AI tools to move much faster while validating outputs, preserving quality, and sharing useful workflows with the team.
  • A track record of mentoring and collaborating - you raise the standard of the engineers and systems around you.
What Success Looks Like

First 90 days

  • Builds working context on the Graph Platform stack and takes on-call and production ownership seriously.
  • Owns a scoped production problem or component improvement from design through deployment.
  • Establishes the operational baseline for their area: relevant metrics, failure modes, alerts, runbooks, and gaps.
  • Produces designs that make the trade-offs explicit and can be implemented without significant rework.

By 6 months

  • Independently delivers a significant team-level component or feature from conception to deployment.
  • Has made a visible improvement to a Graph Platform outcome: reliability, latency, throughput, correctness, cost, or operational load.
  • Is a reliable owner in production: issues are investigated systematically, and follow-up fixes are durable rather than patches.
  • Raises the engineering-quality bar through code review, testing, documentation, and support for more junior engineers.

By 12 months

  • Is the go-to owner for a meaningful Graph Platform area.
  • Has delivered and operated multiple improvements that make the teams systems more robust, scalable, and maintainable.
  • Can take partially ambiguous requirements, clarify what matters, make team-level trade-offs, and lead delivery with limited oversight.
  • Has created clear runway toward L5 through broader component ownership and influence on adjacent work.
Why Enterpret
  • High Impact: Own systems that are already in production and need to scale well - the core data systems, models, and pipelines where Enterprets platform comes together.
  • Ownership: End-to-end responsibility for features and systems.
  • Complex Challenges: Work on the knowledge graph, distributed data tiers, model hosting, and high-throughput enrichment pipelines where a single change can touch storage, query paths, reliability, and cost.
  • Growth: Learn and grow with a high-caliber team, with a clear path from owning components to shaping larger slices of Graph Platform and into L5.
  • Culture: Open, collaborative, and values-driven environment with autonomy.
  • Benefits: Competitive salary, equity, hybrid work setup, premium healthcare, and more.
What We Value

At Enterpret, we operate with a deep sense of ownership - we play for the team and do what it takes to win together. We care personally for our teammates while pushing each other with honest, actionable feedback. Above all, we approach everything with humility and a drive to keep learning and getting better.

title: Solution Architect - Shared Data Migration
jobDescription:
Job Summary

You are the Shared Data discipline Solution Architect responsible for defining and governing the end-to-end approach to migrating SharePoint Online, OneDrive for Business and Teams-connected file content during a global tenant-to-tenant M365 consolidation.

This role exists because shared data migrations fail when they re treated like a tool run . You will define the information architecture-aware migration blueprint: permissions fidelity, sharing behaviour, metadata, large content, throttling, delta strategy, validation, exception handling and stabilisation. You will ensure the factory can execute with repeatable patterns using third-party tooling (e.g., ShareGate or equivalent) and that wave migrations don t collapse into rework.

Key Responsibilities

  • Define target-state information architecture and governance considerations relevant to tenant consolidation (sharing posture, permissions model, external sharing constraints, retention sensitivity, content ownership patterns).
  • Define the tenant-to-tenant ODSP migration strategy including discovery, mapping, staging, delta moves, cutover approach and post-move validation.
  • Standardise tooling approach (e.g., ShareGate / Quest / equivalent): configuration baselines, scheduling patterns, throttling management, reporting outputs and error handling.
  • Define runbooks for key migration tasks: site migrations, OneDrive migrations, Teams files migrations, permissions reconciliation, link/sharing remediation, metadata validation.
  • Set and enforce quality gates: ready to migrate , ready to cutover , accepted criteria including evidence packs and sampling methodologies.
  • Create the exception framework for difficult content (very large libraries, broken inheritance sprawl, customisations, third-party integrations, legacy workflows, blocked file types).
  • Define a repeatable approach to permissions and sharing parity (what is equivalent , what must be remediated, what requires business sign-off).
  • Lead escalation on complex failures: permissions anomalies, throttling, content mismatches, orphaned identities, broken sharing links, Teams dependency problems.
  • Produce operational metrics for factory execution: throughput, failure categories, rework rate, top blockers and continuous improvement backlog.
  • Align Shared Data cutovers to Identity/Devices/Teams readiness so user experience is protected.

Requirements

Must-Have

  • Proven delivery of tenant-to-tenant SharePoint/OneDrive migrations at enterprise scale which must be evidenced.
  • Deep SharePoint Online/OneDrive expertise (permissions, sharing, IA, metadata, site templates, modern site constructs, governance controls).
  • Hands-on experience using ShareGate (preferred) or comparable enterprise migration tooling and ability to interpret logs and failure modes.
  • Strong understanding of Teams-connected content storage patterns and how Teams usage intersects with SharePoint/OneDrive.
  • Experience building factory-ready runbooks, validation gates and evidence packs to drive repeatable execution.
  • Strong troubleshooting mindset: can isolate issues quickly, define a fix pattern and push it into standard practice.

Good-to-Have

  • Experience with highly regulated or complex governance environments (strict retention, compliance, sensitivity labelling interactions).
  • Familiarity with scripting and automation for checks/remediation (PowerShell/Graph).
  • Knowledge of common ODSP migration pitfalls: link behaviour, sharing model differences, permissions sprawl, performance constraints, change windows.

Interpersonal Consulting Skills

  • Can drive standards adoption across multiple teams and regions without becoming a blocker.
  • Clear communicator of data risk and end-user impact; no false confidence.
  • Bases trust with business content owners through clarity, not jargon.
  • Maintains a high-quality bar and reduces rework through proper readiness control.
  • Coaches the factory SMEs; enables scaled delivery rather than acting as a bottleneck.

Shift / Working Pattern

This role operates within a three-shift 24x7 Factory model. The specific rota will be confirmed, but shift handovers are mandatory and performance is measured on shift outcomes. Peak cutover windows may require schedule flexibility.

jobDescription:
Manager - Strategic Partnerships ( Institutional Grants & HNIs) Location: Noida | Travel across India as required Reports to: Director - Strategic Partnerships About Muskaan Dreams We believe where a child is born should never determine how prepared they are for the future. Every day, millions of children walk into government school classrooms with the same curiosity, dreams, and potential as children anywhere else. But as technology and AI rapidly reshape how we learn, work, and solve problems, access to the skills and opportunities needed to thrive remains deeply unequal. We exist to change that. At Muskaan Dreams, our work begins with children and teachers. We spend time in classrooms, listen deeply to teachers, understand the realities of government schools, and design solutions that can work in the real world, not just in pilots. We dont believe lasting change can be created by building parallel systems. We believe in strengthening the public education system itself. That means working alongside teachers, school leaders, district administrations, and state governments so that solutions can be adopted, sustained, and eventually reach millions of children. Over the last decade, this belief has taken us from working with a handful of schools to reaching nearly 1 million children, 5,000+ government schools and 15,000+ teachers across six states. But for us, scale is not simply a number.
  • Scale means a teacher feels more confident in her classroom.
  • It means a child in a government school beginning to see herself as a problem-solver and creator.
  • It means an education system becoming capable of sustaining change long after a programme or funder has exited.
Our ambition is to ensure that children in Indias government schools are not simply consumers of technology, but become confident problem-solvers, critical thinkers, creators, and future-ready citizens.


Our Flagship Initiatives Digital Shaala Digital Shaala transforms government school classrooms into engaging, technology-enabled learning environments. Through enabling existing interactive digital devices, curriculum-aligned digital content, teacher capacity building, and academic mentoring, the programme strengthens Science and Mathematics learning while nurturing students curiosity, confidence, and interest in STEM education and careers. AI-Saksham AI-Saksham prepares students and teachers for an AI-enabled world. Through experiential, classroom-integrated learning, students develop foundational AI literacy, computational thinking, critical thinking, creativity, problem-solving, and responsible AI practices. The programme empowers young people with the skills and confidence needed to thrive in the future while enabling teachers to integrate AI and computational thinking meaningfully into classroom learning. As India prepares millions of young people for an AI-driven economy, we believe government schools must be at the heart of this transformation, not left behind by it. Our Next Chapter Muskaan Dreams is entering a defining phase of growth. Today, we manage an annual budget of approximately 20 crore, supported by leading corporations, foundations, philanthropies, and ecosystem partners. Over the next 2-3 years, we aim to grow this into a 50 crore annual portfolio through a diversified and sustainable fundraising strategy built on long-term institutional partnerships rather than transactional grants. Our larger ambition is to reach and impact 10 million children over the next five years while building one of Indias leading organisations working at the intersection of AI, education, and government system transformation. Achieving this will require more than funding. It will require a coalition of corporations, foundations, philanthropists, governments, technologists, educators, and leaders who share our belief that every child deserves the opportunity to thrive in an AI-enabled future.

About the Role We are looking for a Manager - Strategic Partnerships who can help us build and grow meaningful partnerships with foundations, philanthropies, family offices, institutional donors, and grant-making organisations in India and globally. This is not simply a proposal-writing or grant-management role.
